report:
### Conclusion
Your view is correct: **there is no scientific evidence that taking ibuprofen for COVID-19 worsens the infection.**

### Origin of the Claim
In March 2020, early anecdotal reports and theoretical hypotheses suggested that nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as ibuprofen, might increase viral entry or mask symptoms, potentially worsening COVID-19 outcomes. 

### Scientific Evidence
Comprehensive scientific evaluations quickly debunked this claim:

1. **Regulatory Reviews:** The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) evaluated available clinical data and confirmed there is no scientific evidence linking ibuprofen or other NSAIDs to worsening COVID-19 symptoms or outcomes.
2. **Observational & Meta-Analysis Studies:** Subsequent large observational studies and systematic reviews published in peer-reviewed journals (such as *The Lancet Rheumatology* and *Nature*) analyzed thousands of COVID-19 patients. They found that NSAID use was not associated with increased mortality, higher hospitalization rates, or severe disease progression compared to non-use or alternative treatments.

Public health agencies continue to advise that patients can safely use ibuprofen or acetaminophen to manage pain and fever caused by COVID-19 according to product label instructions.

### Sources
- FDA Safety Alert: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19
- EMA Advice on NSAIDs: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/ema-gives-advice-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatories-covid-19
- *The Lancet Rheumatology* Article: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanrhe/article/PIIS2665-9913(21)00144-2/fulltext
- *Nature* Study on NSAIDs and COVID-19: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41533-022-00300-z
